Going out: Cinema

Minotaur Out now Director Andrey Zvyagintsev cements his reputation as one of the greats, with an impeccably crafted take on Claude Chabrol’s The Unfaithful Wife. Relocated to a Russian town where the government is conscripting men into the Ukraine war, it follows Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) as he discovers his wife is having an affair.

Focker- in-Law Out now Robert De Niro, Ben Stiller and Teri Polo reprise their roles in the Focker franchise, while Ariana Grande plays the new fiancee to Pam and Greg’s beloved son Henry Focker. Per franchise lore, the interloper must be put through her paces to ensure she is worthy of a place in the circle of trust.

Hexed Out now From Le Morte d’Arthur to Harry Potter, stories of young people figuring out their connections to hidden magical worlds remain popular. Disney’s latest take on the topic sees young Billie Doe’s newly discovered powers take her from suburbia into a world of witches, magic and family secrets.

Who Is Still Alive Out now A large-scale black-and-white map of Gaza is the central organising device of this documentary, which contains no actual footage of Gaza, but uses the map as a framework for nine refugees from the region to give voice to their testimony. Directed by Nicolas Wadimoff, it premiered at the Venice film festival. Catherine Bray
Going out: Gigs

blocks.alt: Saxophonist Tony Kofi performs with harpist Alina Bzhezhinska on stage
blocks.caption: Harping on … Alina Bzhezhinska with saxophonist Tony Kofi. Photograph: Imago/Alamy

blocks.text: Alina Bzhezhinska & Tony Kofi Peggy’s Skylight, Nottingham, 28 November; Jazz at Crookes, Sheffield, 29 November Harpist Alina Bzhezhinska has been making waves as a true original. Her subtle, soulful and often thrilling partnership with Ornette Coleman-influenced saxophonist Tony Kofi entrances jazz aficionados and newcomers alike. John Fordham

Jessie Ware 28 November to 5 December; tour starts London Podcaster and pop star Jessie Ware takes April’s sumptuous sixth album Superbloom to arenas. Featuring slow-burn singles such as I Could Get Used to This and the title track, it also tips into sweaty boudoir vibes on Ride and Mr Valentine, so expect some decadent rump-shaking both on and off stage. Michael Cragg

Bryson Tiller 1 to 9 December; tour starts Dublin The Kentucky-born rapper and singer celebrates his recent double album Solace & the Vices, and his 2015 breakthrough record, Trapsoul, on this arena tour. Keep an ear out for Trapsoul’s slow-moving heater Don’t, which has topped 2bn streams. MC

Saariaho’s Adriana Mater London Coliseum, 28 November to 12 December Three years on from her death, the groundbreaking Finnish composer’s 2006 opera about war and motherhood receives its first full UK staging, directed by Annilese Miskimmon. Amin Maalouf’s libretto is performed in a new English translation by the composer’s son, Aleksi Barrière. André de Ridder – ENO’s incoming music director – conducts. Flora Willson
Going out: Art

blocks.alt: A wooden folding screen collaged with vintage stamps, photos, signs and fabric spells “LOVE”
blocks.caption: Screen prints … Peter Blake’s LOVE. Photograph: Peter Blake/Waddington Custot

blocks.text: Peter Blake Pitzhanger Manor, London, to 18 April Peter Blake was one of pop art’s great innovators, and helped shape the course of 20th-century art as a result. This show recreates his west London studio for an intimate insight into his wide-ranging practice.

Anselm Kiefer White Cube Bermondsey, London, to 24 January Expect vast, melancholic, haunted painting by this contemporary German master as he returns to this south London institution for another show of overwhelming and grimly emotional stuff.

The Teän Collection New Art Centre, Salisbury, opens 28 November Salisbury’s finest sculpture gallery is bringing a collection of marine bones to town, with a pilot whale, bottlenose whale and white-beaked dolphin shown in visual dialogue with work by Henry Moore and Dorothy Cross.

Trinity Buoy Wharf drawing prize Arts University Bournemouth, to 12 February Following its launch in London, this annual exhibition of the country’s best drawing – with the main prize this year awarded to octogenarian artist Yvonne Crossley’s depiction of a dancer made of wire – travels to the south coast. Eddy Frankel
Going out: Stage

blocks.alt: One Day poster: a couple embrace laughing, with illustrated London skyline silhouettes behind them
blocks.caption: Timeless romance … One Day.

blocks.text: The Little Match Girl Wilton’s Music Hall, London, 3 December to 2 January Arthur Pita’s charmingly eccentric show mixing music, song and dance is based on Hans Christian Andersen’s tale of a little girl freezing in the snow. If that sounds like a tearjerker, the mood is lifted by Frank Moon’s live soundtrack and a surreal sense of magic, wonder and humour. Lyndsey Winship

Milo Edwards Manchester, 28 November; Leeds, 29 November; Glasgow, 30 November; Newcastle upon Tyne, 1 December; Edinburgh, 2 December Part of a cohort of younger standups who have bypassed TV and found success via podcasting and YouTube, Edwards specialises in big-brained, cool-headed comedy. The 33-year-old’s current show combines edgy observations with material inspired by his late parents’ love letters. Rachel Aroesti

One Day Garrick theatre, London, to 14 March Dex and Em’s timeless love story, immortalised in David Nicholls’s novel, lands in London. There’s music from US crooners Abner and Amanda Ramirez, a brilliant writer-director duo in David Greig and Max Webster, and two musical superstars in Jamie Muscato and Sharon Rose. Miriam Gillinson

Pinocchio Watermill theatre, Newbury, to 3 January Michael Morpurgo’s thoughtful riff on the children’s tale is an intimate and beautifully crafted show, packed with gorgeous puppets, transporting music and flashes of genuine magic. MG

Staying in: Streaming

blocks.alt: In Pride and Prejudice, two women in period costume stand close together, one smiling, one speaking
blocks.caption: Austen power … Hopey Parish and Olivia Colman in Pride and Prejudice. Photograph: Netflix

blocks.text: Pride and Prejudice Netflix, 3 December Every generation (apparently) needs its own adaptation of Austen’s opus; now Dolly Alderton’s millennial iteration has arrived. The cast is first-class – Emma Corrin, Jack Lowden, Olivia Colman – while Alderton’s keen comic sensibility promises a version that won’t skimp on the satire.

Careless Channel 4, 2 December, 9pm Australia-raised writer and longtime Glasgow resident Helen FitzGerald brings her two homelands together for a drama about a Scottish backpacker (Solly McLeod) with a sinister secret who begins caring for a rock star with MS (Richard Roxburgh) during a trip to Sydney. Katie Leung and Robyn Malcolm co-star.

Trinity Netflix, 1 December Waiting with bated breath for Line of Duty? Tide yourself over with this new offering from creator Jed Mercurio, which swaps UK police conspiracies for a military mystery about a naval commander (Gugu Mbatha-Raw) who begins to suspect the imminent threat of nuclear war might not be all it seems.

The Devil’s Hour Prime Video, 4 December In this dizzyingly complex drama, Jessica Raine plays a woman who grows conscious of eternally recurring “time loops” – not so much Groundhog Day as Groundhog life – thanks to Peter Capaldi’s righteous criminal Gideon. Series three sees the pair reunite to track down a child murderer who has evaded detection over multiple lifetimes. RA
Staying in: Games

blocks.alt: In Rayman Legends, an animated man with a big nose looks startled beside a blue creature and horned-helmet girl
blocks.caption: Remake remodel … Rayman Legends Retold. Photograph: Ubisoft

blocks.text: Rayman Legends Retold PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PC ; out 3 December A glossy remake of 2013’s acclaimed Rayman Legends, in which our invisible-limbed hero faces a corrupting darkness. Features new challenges and narrative twists, and a fun co-op mode.

Fall Up Switch, PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S ; out 3 December A cute robot must survive in a dangerous abandoned world, using enemies as handy stepping stones and occasionally warping across the detailed landscapes. It’s the combination of WALL-E and Sonic the Hedgehog that platforming fans have been waiting for. Keith Stuart
Staying in: Albums

blocks.alt: Priya Ragu sits on the floor in a white shirt-dress, its long train pooling around her
blocks.caption: World party … Priya Ragu. Photograph: Bhumika Sharma

blocks.text: Priya Ragu – Madras Out now Written and recorded in Zurich, Goa, Mumbai, Kerala and Chennai, the second album by the Tamil-Swiss singer songwriter playfully skips between genres, utilising a palette that includes south Asian rhythms, disco, R&B and hip-hop. That glorious hotchpotch is showcased on loved-up recent single Finally.

Factory Floor – One Trip Out now A decade after their second album, 25 25, the London trio return. Famed for their uncompromising shows and penchant for raw, post-industrial rhythms, on new songs such as the euphoric Continuation they explore a lighter soundscape.

Peter Gabriel – O/I Out now As with 2023’s I/O, this new opus is split into two, with each song being given Bright-Side and Dark-Side mixes. If you’re thinking: “Wait, aren’t these all on streaming already”, then you’re right; the songs have been released throughout the year to coincide with each month’s full moon and new moon.

Björk – Björk Orkestral With the Hamrahlíð Choir Out now Recorded at Reykjavík’s Harpa Concert Hall in 2021, this live album recasts 11 songs from Björk’s back catalogue. Focused chiefly on songs from 2004’s vocal-heavy Medúlla, and with new arrangements dotted throughout, it’s a beautiful monument to the Icelandic wonder’s experimental drive. MC
Staying in: Brain food

blocks.alt: Double bassist Danny Thompson rests his head affectionately on his instrument
blocks.caption: Ace of bass … Danny Thompson. Photograph: Richard Ecclestone/Redferns

blocks.text: Danny Thompson: 70 Years of Serving the Song BBC Four, 4 December, 10.45pm Featured on more than 1,000 recordings, bassist Danny Thompson played on everything from Nick Drake’s Five Leaves Left to the theme from Thunderbirds. Boasting interviews with Thompson, as well as fascinating archive footage, this film tells his lesser-known story.

Alchemy With Anthony Mason Veteran journalist Anthony Mason takes celebrities to task in this in-depth interview series. Among the artists sharing uncomfortable truths are bestselling novelist Barbara Kingsolver and CMAT.

15 Second Film An ingenious and joyful concept, this Instagram page seeks out famous faces and passersby in New York to write and direct a 15-second short film on the spot. Highlights include mayor Zohran Mamdani on potholes. Ammar Kalia
